The issue was that private escape sequences ($\text{\x1b0}$ to $\text{\x1b?}$) were not being stripped by the ANSI parser in `rich/ansi.py` because the regular expression `re_ansi` used a character class `[@-Z\\-_]` that started at `@` (ASCII 64), missing the range $0\text{--}?$ (ASCII 48–63).

I have updated the character class in `rich/ansi.py` from `([(@-Z\\\\-_]` to `([(0-Z\\\\-_]`. This expansion includes the $0\text{--}?$ range while preserving the original functionality, including the stripping of `\x1b(`.

Verification was performed using a reproduction script that confirmed the original regex failed to strip $\text{\x1b7}$ and $\text{\x1b8}$, while the modified regex successfully stripped them.

The fix is applied to `rich/ansi.py`.

```python
# rich/ansi.py
re_ansi = re.compile(
    r"""
(?:\\x1b\\](.*?)\\x1b\\\\)|
(?:\\x1b([(0-Z\\\\-_]|\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))
    """,
    re.VERBOSE,
)
```
